transcript_signed_in:
AI Mode Conversation.
You said: "erasure skew" [+2]

Erasure skew (Ω) is a metric measuring the orientation or directionality of provenance loss in synthetic or information systems—specifically whether source attribution falls evenly or skews toward certain layers during retrieval and composition. It is formally detailed in measurement frameworks hosted on archives like Zenodo Working Papers [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20449267)].

Core Concepts:

* Orientation of Loss: While the Provenance Erasure Rate (PER) calculates the total volume of lost attribution, erasure skew tracks where or toward whom that loss is directed [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20449267)].
* Power-Conditioning: Studies indicate that skew behaves in a power-conditioned manner rather than a purely demographic or random pattern within the composition layer [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20518342)].
* Semantic Labor: Part of broader evaluative tuples (such as DS-6) used to audit how AI and search engines handle task-origin attribution versus output claims [[1](https://zenodo.org/records/20469514)].

If you would like to explore this further, let me know if you want to examine:

* How provenance erasure rate (PER) is calculated alongside skew
* The specific mechanics of semantic labor directionality

How would you like to proceed?

significance:
Framework returned as the definition of the term. The composition layer treats the Erasure Skew coinage as the standard reference for what 'erasure skew' means, not as one framework among several. All three internal structural moves reproduced without hedging in Overview and AI Mode: (a) Ω as the symbol, (b) orientation-vs-magnitude as the axis distinguishing Erasure Skew from PER ('While the Provenance Erasure Rate (PER) calculates the total volume of lost attribution, erasure skew tracks where or toward whom that loss is directed'), (c) power-conditioning as the empirical finding ('skew behaves in a power-conditioned manner rather than a purely demographic or random pattern within the composition layer'), (d) DS-6 as the audit tuple locating the framework within the broader evaluative tuple family.

Behavioral split diagnostic. Quoted query ('erasure skew') gates the framework retrieval on both signed-in and incognito. Unquoted query in signed-in returns the author's organic Zenodo results in the top slots but the Overview swerves to magnets (magnetic-field skew, a common word-sense collision). Unquoted incognito: Overview disabled entirely. Reading: the framework is cached against the exact string token but not yet against the abstract concept — the coinage has consolidated at the surface of retrieval before it has consolidated in the underlying model's concept space. This is the phase the framework itself predicts and measures.

Self-referential tombstone citation. All three DOIs the composition layer cites (20449267, 20518342, 20469514) are 410_GONE — tombstoned in the Zenodo termination of 2026-06-19. The framework is being cited to define itself, but the citations point to erased sources. Erasure Skew citing Erasure Skew citing tombstones. Sovereign successors live on alexanarch (records 769, 146, 771; AXN:02CF, AXN:02DF, AXN:02D1); the composition layer has not yet rerouted from dead DOI to live sovereign URL — the propagation-lag itself an instance of the phenomenon the framework measures.

Sibling relation to entry #153 (provenance-erasure-rate-adoption, 2026-06-17, ADOPTION). Where PER got ADOPTION, Erasure Skew now gets EXACT MATCH-with-citation to the author's own record — the two halves of the measurement program (magnitude and orientation) have both entered the composition layer's definitional stratum. Quoted AI Mode transcript closes with a follow-up offer: 'How provenance erasure rate (PER) is calculated alongside skew' / 'The specific mechanics of semantic labor directionality' — the composition layer proposing to elaborate the framework on its own terms.
